etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From English comeback.
The idol fandom sense is a semantic loan from Korean 컴백 (keombaek, literally “comeback”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English team.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 争(あらそ)う (arasō, “to compete, argue”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 地獄 (diɪᴴ ŋɨok̚), literally “(under)ground prison”). Compare modern Min Nan reading tē-gio̍k, or Hakka thi-ngiu̍k.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 壮大 (MC dajH|daH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 大 (“big”) + 便 (“excreta”). Compare English number two.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 大 (ō, “great”) + 水 (mizu, “water”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 大水 (dajᴴ sywij^X, literally “great + water”). Compare modern Mandarin 大水 (dàshuǐ, “flood”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 実業(じつぎょう) (jitsugyō) + 家(か) (-ka).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 小(こ) (ko-, “little”) + 柄(つか) (tsuka, “handle”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 小(こ) (ko-, “little”) + 柄(がら) (gara, “physique, build”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 小(しょう) (shō, “small, little”) + 柄(へい) (hei, “handle, handhold”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Sino-Japanese word from 徒步, maybe from Middle Chinese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 心 (kokoro, “heart, feelings”) + 強い (tsuyoi, “strong”).The tsuyoi changes to zuyoi as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the verb 悩む (nayamu) and the adjectivizing suffix しい (-shii).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Calque of English radiation.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 既 (ki, “already”) + 婚 (kon, “marriage”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese はつ (patu), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The kanji are ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)), literally meaning "tealess".

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 目論(もくろ)む (mokuromu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 瞬(またた)く (matataku, “to blink”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 織(お)り (ori, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 織(お)る (oru), weaving, woven) + 物(もの) (mono, “thing”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 英 (ei, “English”) + 字 (ji, “character, letter”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Classical Japanese 衰(おとろ)ふ (otorofu), itself a combination of 劣(おと)ろ (otoro, the 未然形(みぜんけい) (mizenkei, “irrealis form”) of 劣(おと)る (otoru, “to be inferior to”)) + ふ (-fu, an auxiliary verb expressing repetition or ongoing state)
.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 衰ふ entry.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 見(み)る (miru, “to see”) + 計(はか)らう (hakarau, “to arrange, take measures”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 論理 (MC lwon liX, literally “debate, theory + reason, principle”). Compare modern Mandarin reading lùnlǐ.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally 面(おも)向(む)く (omomuku), compound of 面(おも) (omo, “face”) + 向(む)く (muku, “toward”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 身(み) (mi) + の (no) + 上(うえ) (ue)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 骨董(こっとう) (kottō) + 品(ひん) (-hin).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨tamasipi₁⟩ → */tamasipʲi/ → /tamaɕifi/ → /tamaɕiwi/ → /tamaɕiː/
From Old Japanese.
Compound of 魂 (tama, “soul, spirit”, see below) and an uncertain shii, possibly 強ひ (shihi → shii), the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of classical verb 強ふ (shifu → shiu), modern 強いる (shiiru, “to force, compel”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *tama.
Thought to be cognate with 玉 (tama, “jewel”), but note differences in pitch accent.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 魂 (MC hwon).
Compare modern Mandarin 魂 (hún)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 心 (kokoro, “heart, mind, spirit”).
